claims.text: The starting material is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder produced by conventional atomization.
Standard LPBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi produces microsegregation.
Standard LPBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi produces residual stresses.
Standard LPBF processing of AlCrFeNiSi produces processing defects.
AlCrFeNiSi should be processed by LPBF with substrate or chamber preheating at 200–300 °C while other laser parameters are held constant.
Laser power and scan speed can be optimized to obtain high-density LPBF material.
Preheating lowers the temperature differential between the melt pool and the substrate.
Preheating reduces the thermal gradient during solidification.
The reduced thermal gradient makes melt-pool cooling more uniform.
The reduced thermal gradient produces a refined grain structure.
Reducing rapid cooling and heterogeneous nucleation limits compositional segregation.
Reducing the thermal gradient diminishes residual-stress accumulation.
Preheating minimizes microstructural defects such as hot cracks.
Relative to LPBF without preheating, preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have lower residual stress.
Relative to LPBF without preheating, preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have lower segregation and defect densities.
Relative to LPBF without preheating, preheated AlCrFeNiSi will have higher tensile strength and ductility.
The intervention's applicability to other HEA systems or extreme preheat temperatures has not been established.
The optimal preheating temperature and quantitative mechanical-property effects remain to be determined empirically.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis links reduced cooling rate and reduced heterogeneous nucleation to grain refinement, although fewer nuclei and slower cooling do not coherently explain a refined grain structure and may instead favor grain coarsening.

The predicted outcome calls the comparator 'conventionally fabricated' AlCrFeNiSi, but the baseline and experiment actually use LPBF without preheating rather than a conventional bulk-fabrication route.
